The Silent Echo, 2021 Suman Sen (writer director) @sumansen In Mustang - one of the remotest districts of Nepal - childhood is often threatened by “loss, migration, and vanishing certainties.” Here, geography dictates destiny. When confronted by this harsh landscape, what do children dream of? What brings them joy, and how far do they travel for it? ‘The Silent Echo’ is director Suman Sen’s attempt to “listen to children growing up in a landscape where nature is both guardian and threat.” The film follows the journey of four young friends from Mustang who are determined to navigate the practical obstacles to achieve one big dream - winning a band competition in a distant town. Despite the bleak conditions, the children share inner worlds which remain tender and playful. #nepal #girlhood

This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. 🇳🇵 WELCOME TO DASHAIN! Nepal’s biggest and most important Hindu festival, celebrated over 15 days! And ICONICALLY, it celebrates the victory of a powerful goddess over evil. 💅 According to Hindu mythology, Durga, the goddess of strength, courage and protection, battled the evil buffalo demon Mahishasura for nine days before defeating him on the tenth. A whole festival celebrating female power? I’M OBSESSED. 📍 Kathmandu Durbar Square — the historic heart of Kathmandu, home to centuries-old temples and palaces, many of which were badly damaged in the devastating 2015 earthquake and have since been restored. 👑 The Living Goddess (Kumari): Nepal has a tradition of worshipping a real-life young girl as the living embodiment of the goddess Taleju. The current Royal Kumari is just THREE YEARS OLD! She’s selected from a Buddhist family and revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. ❤️ Tika: During Dashain, families come together as elders place a red mixture of rice, yoghurt and vermilion on their loved ones’ foreheads, offering blessings for health, happiness and prosperity. And this is only the beginning of my Nepal adventure… In just a few days, this 34-year-old hag will be attempting to summit Mera Peak at 6,476 metres (21,247 ft) in the Himalayas! 🏔️ No gear, no idea, but plenty of ambition. Follow along to see if I make it to the top! VAMOS! 🇳🇵#solotravel #digitalnomadlife #fulltimetravel #lifeinyour30s
